liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Easy Wind** (1 review): Easy Wind was performed for the first time, featuring a notable jam section [7]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Dark Star lasted six minutes fifty-five seconds, noted as a very brief live version [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Casmic Charlie**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Easy Wind [15]

## The recordings

- **gd69-08-21.sbd.cotsman.13850.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 17 songs; 93 min; rated 4.29/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: The recording quality is described as crispy, particularly for the song Morning Dew; The tape appears to run out just as the song Cosmic Charlie ends [1][3]
- **gd1969-08-21.sbd-part.tremblay.1170.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 50 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: The overall sound quality is considered good, despite the mellow nature of the performance [9]

## Around the show

- Jazz musician Charles Lloyd played flute and tenor saxophone during the performance [5]
- The band seemed to be recovering from Woodstock, which occurred just four days prior [7]
- The stage atmosphere was loose, with Jerry's voice sounding beautiful during Doin' That Rag [8]
- The Aqua Theatre was a floating stage on Green Lake, now replaced by a concrete amphitheater [12]
- The scheduled August 20 show at El Roach rained out, moving the band to the Aqua Theatre [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-08-21.sbd.cotsman.13850.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by JCotsman; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Sound Forge software was used for normalization and minor edits on the tape [1]
- **gd1969-08-21.sbd-part.tremblay.1170.sbeok.shnf**: source: S:Cm,C,D,CDR [Soundboard -> Bear's Cassette master -> Cassette -> DAT -> CD] [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Green Lake Aqua Theatre, Seattle Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1969/artwork/green-lake-aqua-theatre-seattle-poster) [16]
- Fan art by Jordan: [Aqua Theater! | Wallyhood](https://www.wallyhood.org/2009/04/aqua-theater/) [17]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Green Lake Aqua Theatre - August 21, 1969](https://www.dead.net/show/august-21-1969) [18]
- Fan art by johnsdeadart.blogspot.com: [John's Custom Grateful Dead Album Cover Art](https://johnsdeadart.blogspot.com/2017/05/blog-post_47.html) [19]
